dating_evidence: Imperial Airways Ltd. operated from 1924 until 1939, when it merged into BOAC; Croydon was the 'Airport of London' in this era.
Lloyds and National Provincial Foreign Bank Ltd. existed between 1918 and 1955.
Wagons-Lits/Cook reflects the association of the Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-Lits and Thomas Cook & Son, which began in 1928.
'Basle', the English spelling of Basel, was standard in British usage at the time.
Telegraphic addresses were listed as a primary means of business communication.
historical_notes.probable_context: An English-language directory of Swiss and British firms involved in Anglo-Swiss trade, possibly issued by a chamber of commerce or trade promotion body.
notable_firms: Sandoz, Geigy and Ciba (Society of Chemical Industry in Basle) were the major Basel dye and chemical firms. They later merged to form Ciba-Geigy (1970) and Novartis (1996).
Clayton Aniline Co. in Manchester was the British subsidiary of Ciba, which explains its telegram address «Ciba».
Aluminium-Industrie-Aktien-Gesellschaft, Neuhausen, was the forerunner of Alusuisse.
Swiss Bank Corporation (Schweizerischer Bankverein) later merged with Union Bank of Switzerland in 1998 to form UBS.
